history.text: Hey, I'm Flow — I'll be taking your interview today. Please start with a short introduction.
Hi, I’m Ken. I’ve been a backend developer for five years.
Got it. Five years as a backend developer is solid. What motivates you to pursue this software engineering role now?
Not much, really. Just exploring options.
Okay. Exploring options can be a good strategy. Can you share a piece of work you personally drove and a key decision you made during that process?
I built a claims batch pipeline. Made decisions on data processing efficiency.
Okay. You built a claims batch pipeline. What specific actions did you take to improve data processing efficiency?
Okay. You mentioned optimizing queries. What was the impact of that optimization on performance metrics?
It cut processing time by about twenty percent.
Okay. It cut processing time by about twenty percent. In this role, what aspect of day-to-day work are you looking to experience more of compared to your current position?
Not sure. Just want to see what's different.
Fair — that's better than guessing. You want to see what's different. Start with what the task was, and just take it one step at a time.
Yeah, that makes sense. Just figuring things out.

Thanks, Ken. The part about "Optimized queries, reduced redundant computations" is the kind of specific that lands. Your written feedback is on your dashboard in a minute. That's the end of the interview — take care.
